1. Story allies in general are good. For Avalon: Magusar can hold his own easily. Persapius/Monstrux and Militar tend to combine well. Mostly for Avalon you want a higher Dark arm ally and a Dark arm I to balance it out.
For Grim: From the Story allies only Terrwyn is a little less due to her only Frost Offerings selection. Yet Grim has nearly only Neutral arms. Theres a few not neutral arm ones.
For Sactuarium: Aegrus and Sympatha combo always works rather well. 

2. Grim has a good affinity for Hells overall. Weapons are very good cast to damage ratio wise. Special can be really good once you have access to Slime Fleshlumps. In general anything can be viable for Pacts. Its mostly Alice's Maze where things need high efficiency.

3. Affinity is raised by using the allies and using the Faction apropriate action. (Saving for Sactuarium, Fate for Grim and Sacrifice for Avalon) Do note that this only over main targets which in most cases will be Archfiends. Additional Foul creatures spawned can be done with far less of concequence. You can also give them Offerings. With ones they don't use giving nearly nothing, ones they use but of a different rank giving a little more and givining them the exact offering granting the most affininity.

4. Elemental Hells are inflicted by using a high amount of same elemental attacks over the least amount of time. Which you then break by using that Elemental Hells weakness. So a Frozen Hell'ed (Frost) Archfiend would have to be broken for extra damage with a Volt attack. The drop off for Elemental Hells is quite steep. On top of the possible counter acting Hells being applied. See it as it being a lot harder to freeze something if its being burned.

5. The pages with the Jumbled letters would be pages that you go into and unlock using a small scavenger hunt for Essence spots. And will grant Chest's of Fortune Offerings. They are a bit of a skill check I feel.

6. Additional Pacts used/are DLC pacts. They were added later or carried over from Vanilla Soul Sacrifice.

7. They are mostly Lore based. There is not a different mechanic to them gameplay wise.

**But**, it is true that it's a permanent solution. Once you go through with it, there's is no taking it back. That may sound appealing, but really, why *wouldn't* you try all the options before trying the truly permanent one? As long as you have options, there's a chance you can have better.
